items.title: Can LLMs Time Travel? Enhancing Temporal Consistency in Legal Agentic Search through Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: While large language models (LLMs) augmented with agentic search capabilities show promise for legal reasoning, they overlook a fundamental constraint that applicable law must match the temporal context of each case, as retroactive application of statutes violates core legal principles and leads to erroneous conclusions. Our observations reveal that current legal LLMs suffer from temporal bias anchored to their training cutoff, while search agents rarely incorporate temporal constraints into queries, and that web search alone cannot provide the precise statute and precedent citations that legal reasoning demands. To address these challenges, we propose LegalSearch-R1, an end-to-end reinforcement learning framework that pairs local statute RAG for precise article matching with online web search for broader legal knowledge, trained on temporally-indexed data spanning multiple amendment periods to enforce temporal consistency. Extensive experiments on our benchmark covering 13 legal tasks demonstrate that our 7B-parameter agent outperforms state-of-the-art deep research frameworks and specialized legal LLMs by 12.9% to 29.8%, surpasses baselines by 57.7% to 80.3% on temporal consistency, and exhibits robust out-of-domain generalization. The code and data are available at https://github.com/AlexFanw/LegalSearch-R1.
items.institution: HKUST, Tsinghua University, University of Waterloo
items.summary_cn:
## 文章做了什么
- **背景**：大型语言模型（LLM）结合代理搜索能力在法律推理中展现出潜力，但法律推理有一个核心约束：适用的法律必须与案件的时间背景相匹配。追溯适用法律违反了核心法律原则，会导致错误结论。
- **已有工作为什么解决不了**：现有的法律 LLM 存在基于训练截止日期的“时间偏差”；搜索代理很少在查询中纳入时间约束；且单纯的网页搜索无法提供法律推理所需要的精确法条和判例引用，导致在处理跨越不同法律修订期的案件时出现时间不一致性。

## 文章的核心贡献点
- **提出了一个**名为 LegalSearch-R1 的端到端强化学习框架，该框架将用于精确法条匹配的本地法规 RAG 与用于获取更广泛法律知识的在线网页搜索相结合，并在跨越多个修订期的时间索引数据上进行训练，以强制实现时间一致性。
- **挑战1：时间偏差与检索不精确**。现有模型受限于训练数据截止时间，且通用搜索难以定位特定版本的法条。论文通过引入本地法规 RAG 进行精确的法条版本匹配，并结合时间索引数据进行强化学习训练，使模型能够感知并选择正确时间点的法律依据。
- **挑战2：通用知识与专业引用的平衡**。单纯依赖网页搜索缺乏法律所需的严谨引用，而仅靠本地库又缺乏广度。论文通过混合架构，利用在线搜索补充背景知识，同时依靠本地 RAG 确保核心法条引用的准确性和时效性，并通过 RL 优化代理的搜索策略以协调两者。

## 实现与部署，evaluation 结果，要有和相关工作对比
- **实现与部署**：构建了一个包含 13 项法律任务的基准测试集，涵盖多个法律修订时期。使用 7B 参数量的模型作为基础代理。
- **评估结果**：
    - 在整体性能上，LegalSearch-R1 比最先进的深度研究框架和专业法律 LLM 高出 12.9% 到 29.8%。
    - 在时间一致性指标上，比基线方法高出 57.7% 到 80.3%。
    - 表现出强大的域外泛化能力。
- **对比**：显著优于现有的通用搜索代理和未针对时间一致性优化的法律专用模型，证明了引入时间约束和强化学习在法律场景下的必要性。

#### 总结
本文指出了当前法律 AI 代理在处理时间敏感性法律问题时的重大缺陷，即忽视法律修订的时间效力。通过提出 LegalSearch-R1，结合本地精确检索、在线广泛搜索以及基于时间索引数据的强化学习，有效解决了法律推理中的时间不一致问题，大幅提升了法律问答的准确性和可靠性，为法律领域的可信 AI 应用提供了重要参考。
items.summary_en:
## 1. What the Paper Did
- **Background**: Large language models (LLMs) augmented with agentic search show promise in legal reasoning but often overlook a fundamental constraint: applicable laws must align with the temporal context of the case. Retroactive application of statutes violates core legal principles and leads to erroneous conclusions.
- **Why Existing Work Fails**: Current legal LLMs suffer from temporal bias anchored to their training cutoff dates. Search agents rarely incorporate temporal constraints into queries, and web search alone cannot provide the precise statute and precedent citations required for rigorous legal reasoning, leading to temporal inconsistencies.

## Core Contributions
- **Proposed**: LegalSearch-R1, an end-to-end reinforcement learning framework that pairs local statute RAG for precise article matching with online web search for broader legal knowledge. It is trained on temporally-indexed data spanning multiple amendment periods to enforce temporal consistency.
- **Challenge 1: Temporal Bias and Imprecise Retrieval**. Models struggle with time-dependent law versions due to training cutoffs and generic search limitations. The paper addresses this by integrating local statute RAG for exact version matching and using RL on time-indexed data to teach the agent to select legally valid temporal contexts.
- **Challenge 2: Balancing General Knowledge and Precise Citations**. Web search lacks legal precision, while local databases lack breadth. The method combines online search for context with local RAG for authoritative citations, optimizing the agent's search strategy via RL to ensure both accuracy and comprehensiveness.

## Implementation and Evaluation
- **Implementation**: Evaluated on a custom benchmark covering 13 legal tasks with data spanning multiple legal amendment periods. Used a 7B-parameter model as the base agent.
- **Results**:
    - Outperforms state-of-the-art deep research frameworks and specialized legal LLMs by 12.9% to 29.8% in overall performance.
    - Surpasses baselines by 57.7% to 80.3% on temporal consistency metrics.
    - Demonstrates robust out-of-domain generalization.
- **Comparison**: Significantly outperforms existing general search agents and legal-specific models that do not optimize for temporal consistency, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed RL framework and hybrid retrieval approach.

## 4. Conclusion
This paper identifies a critical flaw in current legal AI agents: the neglect of temporal validity in legal statutes. By proposing LegalSearch-R1, which combines local precise retrieval, online broad search, and reinforcement learning on time-indexed data, it effectively resolves temporal inconsistencies in legal reasoning. The approach significantly improves accuracy and reliability, offering a vital step forward for trustworthy AI applications in the legal domain.

items.title: From Model Scaling to System Scaling: Scaling the Harness in Agentic AI
items.abstract: This paper studies the next major bottleneck in agentic AI as system scaling, not only model scaling: the design of auditable, persistent, modular, and verifiable architectures around foundation models. We refer to this shift as scaling the harness: treating the structured execution layer around a foundation model as a first-class object of design, evaluation, and optimization. Although recent large language models enable agents to use tools, retrieve information, maintain memory, and execute long-horizon workflows, evaluation remains largely model-centric, often reducing agents to final-task success while treating memory, retrieval, tool use, orchestration, verification, and governance as secondary implementation details. This framing is increasingly inadequate because agent performance emerges from the interaction among the foundation model, memory substrate, context constructor, skill-routing layer, orchestration loop, and verification-and-governance layer. Together, these components form the agent harness, which translates model capability into long-horizon agent behavior. We study scaling the harness through three core bottlenecks: context governance, trustworthy memory, and dynamic skill routing, together with the orchestration and governance mechanisms that coordinate and constrain them. We further outline a research agenda for harness-level benchmarks that go beyond one-shot task success to measure trajectory quality, memory hygiene, context efficiency, communication fidelity, verification cost, and safe evolution over time. To make the discussion concrete, we develop CheetahClaws: https://github.com/SafeRL-Lab/cheetahclaws, a Python-native reference harness, and compare it with Claude Code and OpenClaw. Our main claim is that future progress in agentic AI will depend as much on system design as on stronger foundation models.
items.summary_cn:
## 文章做了什么
- **背景**：当前 AI 进展的主导叙事是模型缩放（更大的模型、更多的数据），但在代理 AI（Agentic AI）领域，一旦基础模型嵌入到工具、终端、浏览器和记忆存储中，其行为不再仅由模型决定，而是由整个系统决定。
- **已有工作为什么解决不了**：现有的评估和研究 largely 以模型为中心，往往将代理简化为最终任务的成功率，而将记忆、检索、工具使用、编排、验证和治理视为次要的实现细节。这种框架日益不足，因为代理性能涌现于基础模型、记忆基质、上下文构建器、技能路由层、编排循环以及验证与治理层之间的复杂交互。

## 文章的核心贡献点
- **提出了一个“代理 harness”（Agent Harness）的系统缩放框架**：将围绕基础模型的结构化执行层作为设计、评估和优化的首要对象，强调从模型缩放到系统缩放的范式转变。
- **挑战1：上下文治理（Context Governance）**：随着代理执行长 horizon 任务，上下文窗口容易变得杂乱且低效，导致模型注意力分散。**解决方法**：论文提出将上下文构建视为一个独立的治理层，通过优化上下文效率和通信保真度，确保模型接收到的信息是经过筛选和结构化的高质量输入，而非原始数据的堆砌。
- **挑战2：可信记忆与动态技能路由（Trustworthy Memory & Dynamic Skill Routing）**：代理需要在长期运行中维护一致的记忆状态，并根据当前情境动态选择正确的工具或子代理，这涉及状态的一致性和路由的准确性难题。**解决方法**：论文设计了可审计、持久化且模块化的记忆子系统，并结合验证机制来约束技能路由，确保记忆 hygiene（卫生/整洁度）和动作的可验证性，从而提升长期行为的可靠性。

## 实现与部署，evaluation 结果，要有和相关工作对比
- **实现与部署**：作者开发并开源了 **CheetahClaws**，这是一个 Python 原生的参考 harness 实现，旨在使 harness 级别的设计选择显式化。
- **对比工作**：论文将 CheetahClaws 与 **Claude Code** 和 **OpenClaw** 进行了具体对比，分析了不同系统在 harness 设计上的差异。
- **评估视角**：论文并未仅关注传统的单次任务成功率，而是提出了一套 harness 级别的基准测试议程，包括轨迹质量、记忆卫生、上下文效率、通信保真度、验证成本以及随时间安全演化的能力。通过对比分析，展示了系统架构设计对代理整体性能的显著影响，证明了系统设计与基础模型能力同等重要。

#### 总结
本文主张代理 AI 的未来进步不仅依赖于更强大的基础模型，更取决于系统设计的优化。通过提出“缩放 harness”的概念，论文指出了上下文治理、可信记忆和动态技能路由三大核心瓶颈，并提供了 CheetahClaws 作为参考实现。研究呼吁社区从单纯的模型中心评估转向系统级评估，关注代理在长期运行中的过程指标和安全演化能力。
items.summary_en:
## 1. What the Paper Does
- **Background**: The dominant narrative in AI progress has been model scaling (larger models, more data). However, in Agentic AI, once foundation models are embedded into tools, terminals, browsers, and memory stores, their behavior is determined by the entire system, not just the model.
- **Why Existing Work Falls Short**: Current evaluations remain largely model-centric, reducing agents to final-task success rates while treating memory, retrieval, tool use, orchestration, verification, and governance as secondary implementation details. This framing is inadequate because agent performance emerges from the complex interactions among the foundation model, memory substrate, context constructor, skill-routing layer, orchestration loop, and verification/governance layers.

## Core Contributions
- **Proposed a "System Scaling" Framework for Agent Harnesses**: The paper introduces the concept of "scaling the harness," treating the structured execution layer around a foundation model as a first-class object for design, evaluation, and optimization, shifting focus from mere model scaling to system scaling.
- **Challenge 1: Context Governance**: As agents execute long-horizon tasks, context windows become cluttered and inefficient, scattering model attention. **Solution**: The paper proposes treating context construction as a distinct governance layer, optimizing context efficiency and communication fidelity to ensure the model receives filtered, structured, high-quality inputs rather than raw data dumps.
- **Challenge 2: Trustworthy Memory and Dynamic Skill Routing**: Agents must maintain consistent memory states over long periods and dynamically select the correct tools or sub-agents, posing challenges in state consistency and routing accuracy. **Solution**: The authors design an auditable, persistent, and modular memory subsystem combined with verification mechanisms to constrain skill routing, ensuring memory hygiene and action verifiability to enhance long-term behavioral reliability.

## Implementation and Evaluation
- **Implementation**: The authors developed and open-sourced **CheetahClaws**, a Python-native reference harness designed to make harness-level design choices explicit.
- **Comparison**: CheetahClaws is compared against **Claude Code** and **OpenClaw**, analyzing differences in harness design across these systems.
- **Evaluation Perspective**: Rather than focusing solely on traditional one-shot task success, the paper outlines a harness-level benchmarking agenda that includes trajectory quality, memory hygiene, context efficiency, communication fidelity, verification costs, and safe evolution over time. Comparative analysis demonstrates that system architecture design significantly impacts overall agent performance, proving that system design is as critical as foundation model capabilities.

## 4. Conclusion
This paper argues that future progress in Agentic AI depends as much on system design as on stronger foundation models. By introducing the concept of "scaling the harness," it identifies three core bottlenecks: context governance, trustworthy memory, and dynamic skill routing. It provides CheetahClaws as a reference implementation and calls for a community shift from model-centric evaluation to system-level evaluation, focusing on process metrics and safe evolution in long-term agent operations.

items.title: When Do LLM Agents Treat Surface Noise Differently from Semantic Noise? A 68-Cell Measurement Study with a Held-Out Trace-Level Validation
items.abstract: We document an empirical phenomenon in chain-of-thought and ReAct agents driven by ten large language models from seven architecture families: meaning-bearing perturbations (e.g., paraphrase, synonym) alter final answers more often than presentation perturbations (e.g., formatting, reordering) of comparable severity. Across 68 cells spanning GSM8K, MATH, and HotpotQA (1,530 originals and $\sim$11,150 variants), the inconsistency gap averages +19.69 pp after severity matching (paired $t=9.58$, $p<0.0001$), with 64/68 cells positive. The gap survives four severity-proxy audits and remains significant when excluding qwen models (+11.10 pp, $p<0.0001$). Several stress tests fail honestly: cluster-bootstrap significance disappears under stricter assumptions, tractability contrasts do not replicate, cross-architecture generator swaps break per-cell rankings, and a second LLM judge yields only moderate agreement ($κ=0.50$). We then validate the headline effect on a fully held-out 11th model (qwen2.5-14B-Instruct; 1,800 trajectories) and re-test a pre-registered capability$\times$tractability partition, observing a small but positive held-out effect (3/4 cells positive; pooled Welch $t=3.81$, $p=9.6\times10^{-4}$). Using held-out trajectories, we probe four trace-level mechanism signals. Two prior mechanism claims fail to replicate and are explicitly retracted. Two new probes instead support a \emph{stealth-divergence} picture: semantic perturbations often preserve the first action but induce divergence in intermediate reasoning from later steps onward, accompanied by slightly deeper trajectories. We position this as a measurement contribution with held-out replication and a partial trace-level account of how semantic perturbations propagate through agent reasoning. Code, perturbation corpus, raw trajectories, and analysis scripts are released anonymously for review.

items.summary_cn:
## 文章做了什么
- **背景**：随着大语言模型（LLM）代理在复杂推理、数学和检索任务中的部署，输入提示常受到上游模型的重述、模板系统的重排或对抗性扰动的影响。从业者需要了解代理是否将表层噪声（如格式、词序）与语义噪声（如释义、同义词替换）同等对待，还是两者对最终答案的影响存在系统性差异。
- **已有工作为什么解决不了**：现有的扰动鲁棒性研究主要集中在单步语言模型或分类器上（如 PromptBench, CheckList），未能区分“承载意义的扰动”与“呈现形式的扰动”之间的方向性差距，也未深入研究多步代理轨迹中的扰动传播机制。最近的代理基准测试（如 AgentBench）主要衡量原始成功率，而非扰动敏感性。

## 文章的核心贡献点
- **提出了一个**：针对链式思维（CoT）和 ReAct 代理的大规模实证测量研究，揭示了语义扰动比同等严重程度的表层扰动更频繁地改变最终答案的现象，并提供了持留样本（held-out）的轨迹级验证。
- **挑战1：如何量化并验证不同扰动类型对代理稳定性的差异化影响？**
  - **难点**：需要排除扰动严重程度本身的干扰，并在多种模型架构和数据集上证明该现象的普遍性与统计显著性。
  - **解决方法**：构建了覆盖 10 个 LLM、3 个基准测试（GSM8K, MATH, HotpotQA）的 68 个单元格实验，包含 1,530 个原始样本和约 11,150 个变体。通过四种严重程度代理指标进行匹配，发现语义扰动导致的答案不一致率平均高出 19.69 个百分点，且在排除特定模型家族后依然显著。
- **挑战2：如何揭示导致这种差异性影响的内部机制？**
  - **难点**：传统的机制假设可能无法复现，且需要深入代理的内部推理步骤来观察扰动是如何传播的。
  - **解决方法**：使用完全持留的第 11 个模型（Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct）的 1,800 条轨迹进行探针分析。 retract 了两个 prior 机制声明，提出了“隐性分歧”（stealth-divergence）图景：语义扰动通常保留代理的第一步动作，但从第二步开始腐蚀中间推理内容，并导致轨迹略微加深。

## 实现与部署，evaluation 结果，要有和相关工作对比
- **实现与数据**：发布了代码、扰动语料库、原始轨迹和分析脚本。实验涵盖 7 个架构家族的 10 个模型，并在第 11 个模型上进行持留验证。
- **评估结果**：
  - **主要发现**：在严重程度匹配后，语义扰动引起的一致性缺口平均为 +19.69 pp（p<0.0001），68 个单元格中有 64 个为正。
  - **压力测试**：在更严格的假设下，某些聚类 bootstrap 显著性消失；跨架构生成器交换破坏了单元格排名；第二个 LLM 法官的一致性仅为中等（κ=0.50）。
  - **持留验证**：在 Qwen2.5-14B 上观察到较小但正向的效应（+1.08 pp, p=9.6×10⁻⁴）。
  - **机制探针**：语义扰动导致从第二步开始的每步相似度差距扩大（-5.6 至 -10.5 pp），轨迹深度增加 0.17 步。
- **对比相关工作**：不同于 Zhu et al. (2024) 仅报告提示重写降低准确率，本研究明确分离了语义与表层扰动的差距；不同于 Ribeiro et al. (2020) 针对分类器的研究，本研究聚焦于具有工具使用的多步代理；不同于 Sclar et al. (2024) 关注格式对准确率的巨大影响，本研究进一步探讨了语义噪声的深层传播机制。

#### 总结
本文是一项测量贡献，通过大规模实证研究证实了 LLM 代理对语义噪声比表层噪声更敏感。文章不仅通过严格的统计检验和持留样本验证了这一现象的鲁棒性，还通过轨迹级分析揭示了“隐性分歧”机制，即语义扰动在保持初始动作不变的情况下，逐步腐蚀后续推理过程。研究 retract 了部分先前未复现的机制主张，并为输入规范化策略提供了工程启示：应优先关注那些真正改变答案的扰动类型。
items.summary_en:
## 1. What the Paper Did
- **Background**: As LLM agents are deployed for multi-step reasoning, math, and retrieval tasks, input prompts are often perturbed by upstream models or templating systems. Practitioners need to know if agents treat surface noise (formatting, reordering) and semantic noise (paraphrasing, synonyms) equivalently or if they propagate to final answers at different rates.
- **Why Existing Work Falls Short**: Prior robustness studies focused on single-step LMs or classifiers (e.g., PromptBench, CheckList), failing to distinguish the directional gap between meaning-bearing and presentation perturbations in multi-step agent trajectories. Recent agent benchmarks measure raw success rates rather than perturbation sensitivity.

## Core Contributions
- **Proposed**: A large-scale empirical measurement study on Chain-of-Thought and ReAct agents, revealing that semantic perturbations alter final answers more frequently than surface perturbations of comparable severity, validated with held-out trace-level analysis.
- **Challenge 1: How to quantify and verify the differential impact of perturbation types on agent stability?**
  - **Difficulty**: Isolating the effect of perturbation type from severity and proving statistical significance across diverse models and datasets.
  - **Solution**: Conducted a 68-cell study across 10 LLMs and 3 benchmarks (1,530 originals, ~11,150 variants). After severity matching, semantic perturbations caused a +19.69 pp higher inconsistency rate (p<0.0001), remaining significant even when excluding specific model families.
- **Challenge 2: How to uncover the internal mechanisms driving this differential impact?**
  - **Difficulty**: Prior mechanism claims may not replicate, requiring deep inspection of intermediate reasoning steps.
  - **Solution**: Used 1,800 held-out trajectories from Qwen2.5-14B to probe mechanisms. Retracted two prior claims and proposed a "stealth-divergence" picture: semantic perturbations preserve the first action but corrupt intermediate reasoning from step 2 onward, leading to slightly deeper trajectories.

## Implementation and Evaluation
- **Implementation & Data**: Released code, perturbation corpus, raw trajectories, and analysis scripts. Covered 10 models from 7 architectures, with held-out validation on an 11th model.
- **Evaluation Results**:
  - **Main Finding**: A consistent inconsistency gap of +19.69 pp favoring semantic sensitivity (64/68 cells positive).
  - **Stress Tests**: Some cluster-bootstrap significance vanished under stricter assumptions; cross-architecture swaps broke rankings; second LLM judge agreement was moderate (κ=0.50).
  - **Held-out Validation**: Observed a small but positive effect (+1.08 pp, p=9.6×10⁻⁴) on Qwen2.5-14B.
  - **Mechanism Probes**: Semantic perturbations increased per-step similarity gaps (-5.6 to -10.5 pp) from step 2 and increased trajectory depth by 0.17 steps.
- **Comparison**: Unlike Zhu et al. (2024) which only noted accuracy degradation, this work isolates the semantic vs. surface gap. Unlike Ribeiro et al. (2020) focusing on classifiers, this targets tool-using agents. Unlike Sclar et al. (2024) highlighting formatting fragility, this explores the propagation mechanism of semantic noise.

#### Summary
This paper makes a measurement contribution by empirically demonstrating that LLM agents are more sensitive to semantic noise than surface noise. It validates this phenomenon through rigorous statistical testing and held-out samples, while revealing a "stealth-divergence" mechanism where semantic perturbations corrode intermediate reasoning after the initial step. The study retracts non-replicable prior claims and offers engineering insights for input normalization.

items.title: PolyGnosis 2.0: Enhancing LLM Reasoning via Agentic Harness Engineering for Polymarket and OSINT Insight Extraction
items.abstract: This paper introduces PolyGnosis 2.0, a pioneering multi-agent architecture designed to extract predictive intelligence by synthesizing Polymarket anomaly signals with global Open Source Intelligence (OSINT) streams, specifically Global Database of Events, Language, and Tone (GDELT). We define and target "Perspective Mismatches", the narrative divergence between Polymarket sentiment and global media flows, as high-alpha trading signals. Moving beyond generic agentic superiority, we rigorously quantify the efficacy of "Harness Engineering" techniques, including reflection loops, tool-calling, divide-and-conquer partitioning (D&C), and chain-of-thought (CoT), within high-noise financial domains. Our empirical evaluation against human-expert benchmarks reveals that while structural partitioning is mandatory for multi-dimensional alignment, unconstrained terminal reflection actively induces logical drift. Furthermore, we identify a pervasive "consensus bias" across all agent configurations during narrative reasoning, necessitating deterministic validation. Ultimately, we isolate a Pareto-optimal configuration that achieves professional-grade analytical precision while minimizing latency and token overhead, providing a robust blueprint for autonomous intelligence in prediction markets.

items.summary_cn:
## 文章做了什么
- **背景**：预测市场（如 Polymarket）提供了基于共识的公开预测数据，但其数据具有高度复杂性和噪声。仅依靠市场内部数据缺乏外部语境，难以评估市场情绪的真实有效性。
- **已有工作为什么解决不了**：现有的大型语言模型（LLM）若未经辅助，其内部推理难以捕捉专业交易洞察所需的复杂因果关系。单纯依赖模型扩展或通用的智能体优势无法有效解决高噪声金融领域中的结构化推理问题，且缺乏将局部市场信号与全球媒体动态进行系统性交叉验证的机制。

## 文章的核心贡献点
- **提出了一个 PolyGnosis 2.0 多智能体架构**：该架构通过“Harness Engineering”（驾驭工程）技术，合成 Polymarket 异常信号与全球开源情报（OSINT，特别是 GDELT 数据），以提取预测性智能。
- **挑战1：如何从噪声中识别高 Alpha 交易信号？**
  - **难点**：Polymarket 反映的是局部交易者的认知偏差，而全球媒体流（GDELT）代表宏观叙事，两者之间存在巨大的语义和语境鸿沟，直接对比容易产生误判。
  - **解决方法**：定义并 targeting “视角错配”（Perspective Mismatches），即 Polymarket 情绪与全球媒体流之间的叙事分歧。通过多智能体系统专门捕捉这种分歧，将其作为高价值交易信号。
- **挑战2：如何在提升推理能力的同时避免逻辑漂移和共识偏见？**
  - **难点**：复杂的智能体交互（如反思循环）可能导致逻辑漂移，且所有智能体配置在叙事推理中普遍存在“共识偏见”，导致分析结果趋同且可能错误。
  - **解决方法**：严格量化“驾驭工程”技术（反思、工具调用、分治法 D&C、思维链 CoT）的效果。研究发现结构性分治对多维对齐是必须的，但无约束的终端反思会引发逻辑漂移，因此引入确定性验证机制来消除共识偏见，最终隔离出帕累托最优配置。

## 实现与部署，evaluation 结果，要有和相关工作对比
- **实现与部署**：PolyGnosis 2.0 采用多智能体架构，整合了反射循环、工具调用、分治策略（D&C）和思维链（CoT）。系统重点利用 GDELT 数据库作为全球大众媒体动态的综合代理，与 Polymarket 数据进行交叉验证。
- **评估结果**：通过与人类专家基准进行实证评估，结果表明该架构能够达到专业级的分析精度。研究确定了在最小化延迟和 Token 开销的同时实现高精度的帕累托最优配置。
- **对比发现**：
  1. **结构性分治 vs. 通用聚合**：证明结构性分治对于多维对齐是强制性的，优于简单的信息聚合。
  2. **反思机制的双刃剑**：与通常认为反思总能提升性能的观点不同，本研究发现无约束的终端反思会主动诱导逻辑漂移。
  3. **共识偏见**：揭示了在所有智能体配置中普遍存在的共识偏见，强调了确定性验证的必要性，这是许多现有通用智能体框架所忽视的。

#### 总结
PolyGnosis 2.0 通过创新的“驾驭工程”方法，成功解决了在高噪声金融领域利用 LLM 进行专业级推理的难题。它不仅证明了通过精心设计的智能体架构（而非仅仅升级基础模型）可以显著提升推理能力，还具体指出了反思机制的局限性和共识偏见的普遍性。该研究为预测市场中的自主智能应用提供了一个稳健的蓝图，实现了在降低计算成本的同时保持专业分析精度的目标。
items.summary_en:
## 1. What the Paper Did
- **Background**: Prediction markets like Polymarket offer publicly observable, consensus-driven forecasting data. However, this data is inherently complex and noisy. Relying solely on endogenous market data lacks the external context necessary to evaluate the true validity of market sentiment.
- **Why Existing Work Falls Short**: Unaided Large Language Models (LLMs) struggle to capture the intricate causalities required for professional-grade trading insights. Simply scaling models or relying on generic agentic superiority fails to address the structured reasoning needs of high-noise financial domains. There is a lack of systematic mechanisms to cross-validate local market signals with global media dynamics.

## Core Contributions
- **Proposed PolyGnosis 2.0**: A pioneering multi-agent architecture that synthesizes Polymarket anomaly signals with global Open Source Intelligence (OSINT), specifically GDELT, using "Harness Engineering" techniques.
- **Challenge 1: Identifying High-Alpha Signals from Noise**
  - **Difficulty**: Polymarket reflects localized cognitive biases, while global media flows (GDELT) represent macro narratives. Bridging this semantic and contextual gap without generating false positives is difficult.
  - **Solution**: The paper defines and targets "Perspective Mismatches"—the narrative divergence between Polymarket sentiment and global media flows—as high-alpha trading signals, using the multi-agent system to specifically capture these divergences.
- **Challenge 2: Enhancing Reasoning Without Logical Drift or Consensus Bias**
  - **Difficulty**: Complex agent interactions (e.g., reflection loops) can cause logical drift. Additionally, a pervasive "consensus bias" exists across agent configurations, leading to potentially erroneous convergent analysis.
  - **Solution**: Rigorously quantifies the efficacy of Harness Engineering techniques (Reflection, Tool-calling, Divide-and-Conquer, CoT). It finds that structural partitioning is mandatory for alignment, but unconstrained terminal reflection induces drift. Thus, it introduces deterministic validation to mitigate consensus bias, isolating a Pareto-optimal configuration.

## Implementation and Evaluation
- **Implementation & Deployment**: PolyGnosis 2.0 employs a multi-agent architecture integrating reflection loops, tool-calling, Divide-and-Conquer (D&C), and Chain-of-Thought (CoT). It leverages GDELT as a proxy for global media dynamics to cross-validate against Polymarket data.
- **Evaluation Results**: Empirical evaluation against human-expert benchmarks demonstrates that the architecture achieves professional-grade analytical precision. The study identifies a Pareto-optimal configuration that minimizes latency and token overhead while maintaining high accuracy.
- **Comparative Insights**:
  1. **Structural Partitioning vs. Generic Aggregation**: Proves that structural partitioning is mandatory for multi-dimensional alignment, outperforming simple information aggregation.
  2. **The Double-Edged Sword of Reflection**: Contrary to the belief that reflection always improves performance, the study shows that unconstrained terminal reflection actively induces logical drift.
  3. **Consensus Bias**: Reveals a pervasive consensus bias in all agent configurations during narrative reasoning, highlighting the necessity for deterministic validation, a aspect often overlooked in generic agentic frameworks.

## 4. Conclusion
PolyGnosis 2.0 successfully addresses the challenge of professional-grade reasoning in high-noise financial domains through innovative "Harness Engineering." It demonstrates that carefully designed agent architectures, rather than just base model upgrades, significantly enhance reasoning capabilities. The paper critically identifies the limitations of reflection mechanisms and the prevalence of consensus bias, providing a robust blueprint for autonomous intelligence in prediction markets that balances precision with computational efficiency.

items.title: VeriTrace: Evolving Mental Models for Deep Research Agents
items.abstract: Deep research agents face vast, interdependent, and pervasively uncertain information. Existing systems explore what evolving intermediate representations should look like, but leave their evolution to the LLM's implicit reasoning. Without explicit regulation, the intermediate layer is easily contaminated by mixed-quality information and propagates errors along its dependencies, so model scale often ends up substituting for absent regulation. We argue that an agent's mental model should instead evolve through explicit feedback that continuously aligns task understanding with reality, and identify three regulatory loops: interpretive update, deviation feedback, and schema revision. We realise this in VeriTrace, a cognitive-graph framework that explicitly implements the three loops. Using matched Qwen3.5-27B backbones, VeriTrace improves over the strongest matched baseline by 4.22 pp on DeepResearch Bench (DRB) Insight (1.49 pp Overall) and by 5.9 pp Overall win rate on DeepConsult. With Config-DeepSeek, it achieves the strongest reproducible open-source result on DRB.
items.summary_cn:
## 文章做了什么
- **背景**：深度研究智能体（Deep Research Agents）在处理长周期、开放式的科研任务时，面临海量、相互依赖且充满不确定性的信息。为了超越LLM上下文窗口的限制，现有系统通常将中间研究产物（如大纲、证据库、概念池）外部化为一个持久的结构化中间层。
- **已有工作为什么解决不了**：现有的系统（如WebWeaver, OmniThink等）主要关注中间层应该呈现何种形式，但将其演化过程完全留给LLM的隐式推理。由于缺乏显式的调节机制，中间层容易受到混合质量信息的污染，并沿依赖关系传播错误。因此，现有方法往往依赖扩大模型规模来弥补监管缺失，导致效率低下且鲁棒性不足。

## 文章的核心贡献点
- **提出了一个 VeriTrace框架**：这是一种认知图（cognitive-graph）框架，将智能体的中间层视为“心智模型”，并通过三个显式的反馈循环来调节其演化，确保持续对齐任务理解与现实。
- **挑战1：信息噪声与被动积累导致的注意力分散**。难点在于如何从海量混合质量的发现中筛选出对当前任务真正有价值的信息，避免系统被噪声干扰而迷失研究方向。VeriTrace通过“解释性更新（Interpretive Update）”循环解决此问题，新发现不再被被动吸收，而是根据现有模型被分类为确认、矛盾、填补空白或意外惊喜，从而主动塑造可用观察结果。
- **挑战2：错误沿依赖关系的传播与模型僵化**。难点在于当中间层出现偏差或结构不再适应新证据时，如何防止错误扩散并动态调整知识结构。VeriTrace通过“偏差反馈（Deviation Feedback）”和“模式修订（Schema Revision）”循环解决此问题，持续检测任务理解与现实的偏差，并动态重构知识图谱的模式，确保心智模型向健康方向演化。

## 实现与部署，evaluation 结果，要有和相关工作对比
- **实现与部署**：VeriTrace基于认知图架构实现，集成了上述三个调节循环。实验使用了匹配的 Qwen3.5-27B 作为骨干模型，并与 Config-DeepSeek 结合进行测试。
- **Evaluation 结果**：
  - 在 DeepResearch Bench (DRB) 上，使用匹配的 Qwen3.5-27B 骨干，VeriTrace 在 Insight 指标上比最强的匹配基线高出 4.22 个百分点，整体（Overall）高出 1.49 个百分点。
  - 在 DeepConsult 基准测试中，整体胜率提高了 5.9 个百分点。
  - 结合 Config-DeepSeek 时，VeriTrace 取得了 DRB 上最强的可复现开源结果。
- **对比**：相较于 WebWeaver、OmniThink 和 FS-Researcher 等仅关注中间层形式而缺乏显式调节机制的工作，VeriTrace 通过显式反馈循环显著提升了在复杂、不确定性环境下的研究质量和鲁棒性，证明了显式调节优于单纯依赖模型规模的隐式推理。

#### 总结
VeriTrace 提出了一种新的范式，即通过显式的反馈循环（解释性更新、偏差反馈、模式修订）来演化和调节深度研究智能体的“心智模型”。该方法有效解决了现有系统中因缺乏监管而导致的信息污染和错误传播问题，在多个基准测试中取得了优于最强基线的性能，证明了在深度研究中引入显式认知调节机制的重要性。
items.summary_en:
## 1. What the Paper Did
- **Background**: Deep research agents face vast, interdependent, and uncertain information in long-horizon tasks. To overcome LLM context window limits, existing systems externalize intermediate research artifacts (e.g., outlines, evidence banks) into a persistent structured layer.
- **Why Existing Work Falls Short**: Current systems (e.g., WebWeaver, OmniThink) focus on the form of the intermediate layer but leave its evolution to the LLM's implicit reasoning. Without explicit regulation, this layer is easily contaminated by mixed-quality information, propagating errors along dependencies. Consequently, these methods often rely on scaling up model size to compensate for the lack of regulation, leading to inefficiency and poor robustness.

## Core Contributions
- **Proposed VeriTrace**: A cognitive-graph framework that treats the intermediate layer as the agent's "mental model" and regulates its evolution through three explicit feedback loops to continuously align task understanding with reality.
- **Challenge 1: Distraction from Noise and Passive Accumulation**. The difficulty lies in filtering valuable information from massive, mixed-quality findings to prevent the system from losing track of its research state. VeriTrace addresses this via the "Interpretive Update" loop, where new findings are actively classified (confirming, contradicting, gap-filling, or surprising) against the existing model, rather than being passively absorbed.
- **Challenge 2: Error Propagation and Model Rigidity**. The challenge is preventing error spread along dependencies and adapting the knowledge structure when it no longer fits new evidence. VeriTrace solves this through "Deviation Feedback" and "Schema Revision" loops, which detect deviations between task understanding and reality and dynamically refactor the knowledge graph schema, ensuring healthy evolution of the mental model.

## Implementation and Evaluation
- **Implementation**: VeriTrace is implemented as a cognitive-graph architecture integrating the three regulatory loops. Experiments used matched Qwen3.5-27B backbones and were also tested with Config-DeepSeek.
- **Evaluation Results**:
  - On the DeepResearch Bench (DRB), using matched Qwen3.5-27B, VeriTrace outperformed the strongest matched baseline by 4.22 percentage points (pp) on Insight and 1.49 pp on Overall metrics.
  - On DeepConsult, it achieved a 5.9 pp higher overall win rate.
  - With Config-DeepSeek, it achieved the strongest reproducible open-source result on DRB.
- **Comparison**: Unlike WebWeaver, OmniThink, and FS-Researcher, which lack explicit regulation mechanisms, VeriTrace significantly improves research quality and robustness in complex, uncertain environments through explicit feedback loops, demonstrating that explicit cognitive regulation is superior to relying solely on implicit reasoning via model scaling.

## 4. Conclusion
VeriTrace introduces a new paradigm for evolving and regulating the "mental model" of deep research agents through explicit feedback loops (Interpretive Update, Deviation Feedback, Schema Revision). This approach effectively mitigates information contamination and error propagation caused by the lack of regulation in existing systems. It achieves superior performance across multiple benchmarks, highlighting the importance of introducing explicit cognitive regulation mechanisms in deep research tasks.
